To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

cross-functional teams can be a powerful tool for innovation and learning, but the success of cross-functional teams is dependent on the context of the organization, the team, the team's task, and the team's leadership.
the structure and context of the project team and the team’s leadership, as well as the team’s composition and task, influence the team’s learning and innovation.

Cross-functional teams can be an effective way for organizations to share knowledge, develop innovative solutions, and improve organizational performance; and, the effectiveness of a project team is influenced by a combination of organizational structure, project task, and team composition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role that project team composition, leadership, and organizational structure play in shaping the way project teams approach their task and learn from their work.
how teams learn and innovate in organizations.
the ways in which cross-functional teams learn to manage and share knowledge, develop new products and services, and improve processes and organizational performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cross-functional project teams are an essential component of innovation in technology-based organizations.

the cases presented here suggest the importance of a cross-functional team's composition, task, technology, leadership and context on its learning, and that the team's learning is a critical factor in its success.

the project team is a critical component of organizational learning, and that the project team's ability to learn and adapt to new information, new technologies, new markets, and new organizational structures is critical for the success of the organization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

cross-functional teams are a powerful mechanism for knowledge sharing and organizational learning, but that the way teams are organized and managed will have a profound impact on the way they share and use information.
the composition, structure and leadership of cross-functional teams can significantly impact the team's ability to learn and innovate.
the composition and context of cross-functional teams, as well as the task, technology and leadership style of the teams’ leaders, all shape the learning and knowledge sharing of the teams.
The main takeaway from our work is that
technology and innovation managers need to be cognizant of the organizational and project team factors that shape the way cross-functional teams work and learn.
technology and innovation managers should pay close attention to team composition, team development, and team learning.

project managers should consider the ways in which team composition and organizational context shape the way teams work, and how they can leverage the team's composition and context to facilitate learning and knowledge sharing.
